NOT_FROM_THE_CORAL_SCRIPT: analyze_coral_dev8000_budget.py section 4 emits a CORAL budget declaration (deep_coral, gamma=16, 2000 steps) that is hardcoded and unrelated to this arm. It is the Task-A DECAY DETECTOR that is used from that script, applied unmodified; its budget section is not.
budget_confound_removed_by_a_match: A MATCH REMOVES THE BUDGET CONFOUND ONLY. Head initialisation and the gamma-tuning budget still travel with every contrast (7.18) and are not addressed by reading at a matched step.

crossing_resolution.BUT_THE_TRAJECTORY_IS_BATCH_NOISY: the nuclear norm is a per-batch reading and it is not monotone: over steps 25-500 it moves non-monotonically (closest sub-ceiling approach 10.8162 against a ceiling of 10.8413). So the finer cadence resolves WHERE WE LOOKED to +/-25, but the crossing step itself is only as well determined as that noise allows -- a single sharp batch could cross earlier. This is a limitation of the rule as written, recorded rather than corrected, because the rule is pre-registered and was applied as written.

development_run.cadence: every 25 steps to 500 (STATISTICS ONLY), then every 250 (full evaluation)

purpose: the confirmatory budget for folds 1-4, derived by the rule pre-registered in runs/bnm_r6_prereg.json
read_off_rule: train to the budget and read the FINAL checkpoint. R1 -- the last checkpoint -- as pre-registered throughout the project. No label-free selector, no argmax, no smoothing: THE BUDGET IS THE SELECTOR.
rule: budget = 2 x the first step at which normalised ||A||_* reaches 10.8413, the sharpening-only ceiling; NEVER exceeding the declared ceiling of 8000
which_number_is_quoted: the rule-derived budget is not one of the declared arm budgets {1500, 2000, 4000}, so it is quoted ONLY as BNM's own-objective reading -- 'BNM read where its own objective says it is done'. All cross-arm contrasts use MATCHED READOUTS, with 4000 mandatory as the lambda=0 known-null's budget
